Hitched

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two cousins hitch hike half way around the world to convince Ellen to put them on her show

Unique Selling Point:
When Josh and Luke (cousins) where 6 they watched a documentary about a mystical creature that lived in a Congolese jungle. Fast forward 20 odd years and they decided to take 500$ for 100 days and hitch hike to war torn Congo and see if this animal actually exists. Obviously it didn’t but they had the most insane ride regardless. After returning home they decided to do a second trip, this time the mission is to get onto the Ellen show. Again with almost no money they committed to a 7 month trip across Africa and Europe and into LA. They whole trip is being documented and almost become like a daily journal to Ellen. Sadly in 7 months Ellen never replied to all their messages, videos, hashtags. But they made it to LA and are currently camping near the beach still hoping to get onto Ellens couch.

Their journey is extreme they do things that seem so insanely unsafe, but they just laugh and take every speed bump in their stride. This trip took them through Sudan, unrest in Ethiopia and subzero temps in a tent in Russia. Luke also got engaged along the way

Everyone can learn something about life from the hitched boys. Even if its just that "It ain't about the destination, its about the journey"

02:05 Docuseries Hitched Jordan: Hi my name is Jordan
Luke: my name is Luke
02:07 Voice over They covered 10 countries in 107 days with 72 lifts and living on a dollar a day
02:13 Documentary Luke: don’t want to fall asleep and fall off

02:16 Macfarlane interview Mac: Did you find the dinosaur let’s start there?

Luke: We can’t give you the end of the documentary you have to watch it.

02:27 Jordan and Luke Jordan: So we thought the only way we were going to make it as documentary filmmakers is to take this thing international so we figured we needed to get to LA to Hollywood

02:40 Documentary Luke: so we have got 4 choices
1 – Frowdo
2 – Morgy
3 – Kimsta
4 – Ellen

Luke: yeah and Ellen DeGeneres won the votes so then cool that’s the direction we are going and we are going to hitchhike to Ellen DeGeneres and show her our first season.
02:54 Voice over Jordan and Luke with filmmaker Don, hitched 14 countries in 8 months to get to LA and onto the Ellen show. They were posting live about every experience and getting south Africa to share their post #Ellen
03:09 Luke: hey Ellen it’s me Luke again, just like 8 to show you what I have to deal with on a daily basis these 2 plonkers think they found a pyramid
03:18 Macfarlane Macfarlane: Why do you choose hitchhiking as a mode of transport I mean there are many other ways to decide to do this trip?
Jordan: for us hitch hiking kind of out of this necessity of just being broke and not having money. Our moms are actually hitchhikers themselves back when they were young so like they used to hitchhike all over Southern Africa and whatnot that we grew up with that sort of background of. That’s kind of what you do you know. within the realms of travel it's one of the most authentic experiences you can have. That's just because every day you just bumping into your everyday person in that country

Luke: we were on our way to Ethiopia on bikes but we had visa fails

04:19 Documentary Luke: Yoh so sick to be off that thing, I started to think we would never get off so
04:24 Voice over They have been bitten by every insect known to man
04:26 Documentary Luke: amongst all these bites I have got this one on my elbow that is becoming really sore by the day. From what we understand its some kind of acid bug

04:39 Documentary Luke: I’ve already fallen once and if I fall who can help me?
04:43 Voice over Lost their tents on some zero temps in Russia and landed up in war zone
04:48 Luke: We just so happen to have done trips that go through areas where in those times all voices in media and stuff like that are telling you hey don't go there for example in the Congo. We went through that Kiva you rebel area
05:00 Documentary Local: They kill and they run
Luke: and you say this was last week?
Local: yes
Luke: it’s at times like this that I ask myself why I’m doing these kind of trips
05:12 Luke: This trip we went through in Sudan and literally about two weeks after that hole Sudan massacre
05:20 Documentary Luke: it’s quite peaceful at the moment to us it just seems fine but for everyone was saying last week it was hectic in all the roads there’s so much military present
05:20 Interview Luke: you could see people were like really aching inside but at the end of the day it's still just a mother trying to feed her kids and that kids got to go to school and so you’re on a bus and you just get past that baby you baby-sitting for two hours there's no asking about that you just do it because everyone is rallying to just get through the day you know.
Mac: Was there a time though were you felt like our lives are in danger let’s not take a chance.
Jordan: we've had times were definitely your adrenaline pumping and your heart's going.
06:02 Voice over While hiking with a pair of slipslops, Luke fell off the side of a cliff face and went into the waves below disappearing from sight
06:09 Documentary Jordan: We are just sitting here hoping that Luke’s alright

Jordan: it sounds over dramatic but it’s the closest I’ve felt to die
06:40 Interview Luke: that was when you definitely start praying quite a bit.

Mac: at some point though do you miss home?
Jordan: you do have those moments but these something amazing just also about having your whole life in a bag you know

Luke: when people say at home I mean I've got a bag of stuff about a meter by meter at my parents’ house and actually they recently got robbed and say to half of the stuff and it got stolen so now but half a bag That's literally all I had back in Durban.
Jordan: And I think also it's just that that thing of like living on a on a day to day basis and it's really refreshing when you come from a world where you constantly your mind is constantly going.
07:20 Documentary Jordan: good morning Ellen America
Luke: good stuff, home of the brave.
07:29 Interview Mac: Did you guys ever eventually make it onto the Ellen show?
Jordan: No. So we didn't make it onto the show. they were kind of just a little bit on that 50/50 like oh we don't know if we can sort of condone this kind of behavior. Can’t just make a storm and go rash a bunch of celebrities and then you get what you want.
07:47 Documentary Luke: Hi Ellen it’s me Luke I’m not going to lie we haven’t obviously bumped into you in LA, there’s few more people here than I thought
07:53 Jordan: they said they’re gonna go through all of it and get back up on what they can do
Luke: yeah so there is still a small chance
07:59 Documentary Both Ellen
Luke: we are just in Mexico if you decide to bring us back for the show
08:04 Macfarlane link Over and over we’ve been told that society is more disconnected than ever before, we live behind our high walls TV’s and phone screens but these 2 guys are teaching us how to do things totally differently and still have a jol
08:17 Luke: I think one of the biggest mistakes people make in their lives is that when you just think way of life is the norm and like unfortunately that often comes of thinking that your way of life is right. just because that's what you've grown up with. I think just so much prejudice and hatred in the world comes from that view of things that are other to you

Jordan: for me like one of the biggest things learning on this trip was that something like human kindness it doesn't matter what capacity or the level to what you can do it you know with you know good people often relate generosity and kindness to like how much you can give or what you can give you know. it doesn't matter the level to what you can do that it's that it's the act of kindness that changes people.
